title: A projection task that loses the lease is retried until it runs
description:
As an editor, I want a projection task that loses the projection lease to be retried until it runs, so that a change never leaves a public page stale until some unrelated later change.

Observed 2026-11-13 on Machines on Machines: content-actions invocations failed at 14:28, 14:32 and 14:34 UTC with `ProjectionTaskFailed: Projection lease ... waited 10s` while publishes ran.

Findings (origin/develop c17e42ff8):
- Queued item builds (`run_queued_build`, handler.py) wait QUEUED_LEASE_WAIT_SECONDS = 10 s, then enqueue the item durably (`jobs.enqueue`), raise, and Lambda retries once (`addProjectionRetries`, amplify/publication/s3-projection.ts: retryAttempts 1, maxEventAge 1 h, on-failure DLQ). The lease holder drains the queue before letting go. Narrow gap: if the holder's last `queued_items()` check and `after_release` run before the loser's `enqueue`, only the single Lambda retry remains; if that also loses, the item stays in the queue set and in the DLQ with nobody scheduled to build it until some later build drains it. A holder can hold the lease up to the 900 s function limit minus 45 s (drain loop), far beyond 10 s.
- Home-page snapshot (`run_home_page_snapshot_task`, run under the default 120 s lease wait): the dirty list `home-page-dirty#<scope>` is acknowledged only after success, so the changes are not lost, but the Scheduler target has MaximumRetryAttempts 0 (amplify/plugins/home-page/function/handler.py create_snapshot_schedule), Lambda retries once, then the event goes to the projection DLQ, which has no consumer, no re-drive and no alarm. The debounce slot has expired, so nothing schedules another run until the next watched Reference change. Public pages stay stale until then.
- Reproject, reader-snapshot and page-refresh tasks have the same shape: one Lambda retry, then DLQ.

Fix: a task that cannot get the lease leaves its change pending in the lock table (the dirty list for the home page, the queue set for item builds) and a durable trigger for the next run exists before the task fails: the lease holder, on release, reads the pending markers (one GetItem per marker, no scan) and starts exactly one follow-up run per pending marker; a pending marker that outlives the holder's release (the race) is re-armed by the loser itself with an adaptive delay taken from the observed holder expiry (`expiresAt` of the lease), not a fixed wait. Failures after the retry budget raise an alarm on the projection DLQ. Exact-page invalidation only; the follow-up compute runs once per change.

```gherkin
Feature: A projection task that loses the lease is retried until it runs

  Scenario: A task that loses the lease leaves its change pending
    Given another projection holds the site's lease for longer than the task's wait
    When a home-page snapshot task for changed References loses the lease
    Then the changed Reference ids are still listed as pending
    And no change is acknowledged

  Scenario: The next run picks the pending change up
    Given a task lost the lease and left its change pending
    When the lease holder lets go
    Then one follow-up run starts for the pending change
    And that run publishes the page with the change
    And the pending marker is cleared only after the run succeeded

  Scenario: Nothing is dropped when the holder finishes before the loser records its change
    Given a lease holder has already checked for pending work and released
    When a task that lost the lease records its change as pending afterwards
    Then the task arms its own follow-up run
    And the change is published without any further editor change

  Scenario: A queued item build that loses the lease is built by a later run
    Given a Story's page build waited for a busy lease and failed
    When the lease is free again
    Then the Story's page is built and the Story is no longer queued

  Scenario: Retrying never reads a whole table
    Given a site with thousands of References and published Stories
    When a task loses the lease and is retried five times
    Then each retry reads only the pending markers and the changed rows
    And no table is listed or scanned

  Scenario: The retry waits as long as the holder needs, not a fixed time
    Given the lease holder's lease expires in 40 seconds
    When a task loses the lease
    Then its follow-up run is armed no earlier than the holder's expiry
    And a holder that finished early releases and starts the follow-up at once

  Scenario: A change that still cannot run is reported
    Given a task failed past its retry budget
    Then the projection dead letter queue has an alarm
    And the pending change is still listed, so the next run publishes it
```

comments.text: Another occurrence reported 2026-11-13 by the Machines on Machines story session on CLI 5.109.0: a post publish waited about 14 minutes 'waiting for the site to be free' before its page was built, consistent with the lease holder draining and the loser waiting on the lease. Recorded here, not filed separately.
